conditions_for_bcw_dispatch: The CO2 price must exceed the BCW-vs-gas parity price: about 160 $/t for the base case, 124 $/t for the high case, and 214 $/t for the low case.
A cheaper clean firm resource must be constrained. With unconstrained hydro, even $200/t leaves BCW at zero because hydro expands to 3,252 PJ in 2050.
With $200/t and hydro frozen at 2021 activity, SUPBCW reaches the 42.959 PJ cap and PWRBCW produces 11.548 PJ/yr of electricity.

forcing_conditions.carbon_200: EmissionsPenalty 95 $/t for 2021-2025 and 200 $/t from 2026; all other parameters from the BC-base national rollup.
forcing_conditions.carbon_200_hydro_frozen: The carbon_200 forcing plus a TotalTechnologyAnnualActivityUpperLimit on every PWRHYD<zone> equal to its 2021 base-run activity in all years.

limitations: The model has a national SUPBCW cap only. Zonal BC caps (SUPBCWB1/B2) cannot be represented without a model-structure change.
BCW is a national fuel. In the hydro-frozen run PWRBCW dispatches in A1/A2/S1/Q1/Q2/T1/L1, not in B1/B2; the model does not allocate BC residue to BC.

PWRBIO stays at zero in both sensitivity runs because the model's wind cost (about 86.03 $/MWh including the $3/GJ RNW resource placeholder) is marginally below generic BIO (86.28 $/MWh); the generic-BIO bypass is latent, not active.

carbon_200.description: BC base with a $200/t CO2 penalty from 2026
carbon_200.forcing: EmissionsPenalty 95 $/t for 2021-2025 and 200 $/t from 2026; BC-base national SUPBCW rollup unchanged.

carbon_200_hydro_frozen.description: BC base with $200/t CO2 and hydro frozen at 2021 activity
carbon_200_hydro_frozen.forcing: EmissionsPenalty 95 $/t for 2021-2025 and 200 $/t from 2026; every PWRHYD<zone> activity upper limit fixed at its 2021 base-run activity in all years.
